cards.headline: A song of triumph, written for a character the script calls 'the Negro'
cards.snippet: Anthony Newley and Leslie Bricusse wrote 'Feeling Good' for their musical The Roar of the Greasepaint – The Smell of the Crowd. In the show, the character who sings it — a Black outsider the script names 'the Negro' — beats the white leads at their own game and takes the stage in triumph; reviewers called it 'a booming song of emancipation'. Cy Grant sang it on the opening night of the UK tour in August 1964. Nina Simone recorded it in New York in January 1965, in Hal Mooney's arrangement, for her album I Put a Spell on You — and it was not even released as a single.
cards.context: Cy Grant sang it on the UK tour; Gilbert Price took the role on Broadway, and Grant's own jazz recording followed in 1965.

cards.headline: Thirty years an album track — then a Volkswagen ad made it a hit
cards.snippet: For thirty years it stayed an album track, kept alive by singers. Then, in 1994, a British Volkswagen commercial used Simone's recording, and the single finally issued reached No. 40 in the UK. The covers kept coming — Muse's in 2001, Michael Bublé's hit in 2005 — but the original outlasted them: American Songwriter ranked it the greatest Nina Simone song in 2022, the Guardian put it fourth in 2023, and in 2021 it finally received an official video, fifty-six years after Simone recorded it.
cards.context: Its afterlife runs through other people's hits too: Simone's vocal sits at the centre of Jay-Z and Kanye West's 'New Day' (2011).

cards.headline: 'A strong, black woman' — 'and I'm an Asian man'
cards.snippet: This song makes me feel like a strong, black woman, and I'm an Asian man
cards.context: Its most-liked reply blesses the borrowing: 'strength and joy are things everybody should feel.'

cards.headline: Nina Simone sang in her living room — to her mother, in 1983
cards.snippet: She sang in my living room to my mother when I was 18. 1983. I had no ideas who she was at the time. My mother told me one day my dear you will. Today I paid just to listen to her daughter sing her music. My mom is 80 yrs. old my bday gift to her 💕
cards.context: She grew up a county over from Simone's hometown of Tryon, North Carolina — and decades later took her mother, now 80, to hear Simone's daughter Lisa sing her mother's songs.

replies.author: @chrislund5598
replies.text: What a special memory Deidre, that is such an amazing experience few people can tell of such moments.

replies.author: @amyfionna
replies.text: You're were  blessed to have that experience. ❤️

cards.headline: Muse (2001): the cover voted the greatest of all time
cards.snippet: Muse turned the song into widescreen melodrama for Origin of Symmetry (2001) — piano, falsetto and a megaphone passage; issued as a single with 'Hyper Music', it reached No. 24 in the UK. One listener: "This is how you cover a song! Give it a serious breath of new life!"
cards.context: NME's readers put it ahead of Johnny Cash's 'Hurt' and the Beatles' 'Twist and Shout' in 2010; a BBC poll in 2014 placed it ninth.

cards.headline: Perfect Days (2023): the song Wenders saved for the final scene
cards.snippet: The film's final scene: Hirayama, a Tokyo toilet cleaner, begins another workweek at dawn, driving his van and listening to Simone on cassette, as a range of powerful emotions wash over his face.
cards.context: Wenders on Hirayama's cassettes: 'He chooses in the morning exactly what he's going to listen to that day. And it's not random.'
